mainTopic: Cooked donkey hide and טומאה; the placenta and the worry about another fetus; firstborn and קדשים placentas; דרכי האמורי
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבי יצחק נפחא's question about cooked donkey hide. Both טומאת אוכלין and טומאת נבלות seem to be already settled by ברייתות, so the question looks unnecessary. The גמרא answers that the question was about טומאת אוכלין, and donkey hide is different because it is disgusting. Next, on a שליא that partly came out, רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן disagree about when we worry that it belonged to another fetus. After a challenge from רבי ירמיה, the מחלוקת is reworded: רבי אלעזר is the strict one and requires the placenta to be attached to the fetus found inside. A ברייתא about a woman who miscarries supports him. The גמרא then explains why a first-born placenta may be thrown to the dogs: females plus the נדמה make possible בכור males a minority. With קדשים, however, most young are holy, so the placenta must be buried. Finally, אביי and רבא teach that a practice with a real healing purpose is not דרכי האמורי. The גמרא begins to challenge this with a ברייתא about painting a tree red, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the teaching is about carcass impurity, we already learned it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: a teaching about טומאת נבלות would also be unnecessary, because it was already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the teaching was needed for the impurity of carcasses, we already learned that too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a two-part challenge to the question about cooked donkey hide. It already said a question about טומאת אוכלין would be unnecessary, and now it says the same about טומאת נבלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know what רבי יצחק נפחא was unsure about when he asked about cooked donkey hide. It lists the two possible kinds of impurity and argues that each one is already settled by an existing ברייתא. If both are settled, the question seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If (introducing one possible option)
The impurity of an animal carcass, passed on by touching or carrying it

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different impurities here. טומאת אוכלין is the impurity that any food can receive. טומאת נבלות is the much stronger impurity of a dead animal's flesh. A part can count for one and not the other.

phrases.english: If it is for the impurity of carcasses
– we already learned it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'if food impurity, we learned it' challenge that began just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יצחק נפחא's question about cooked donkey hide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible legal uses, food impurity and carcass impurity, are already covered by other sources, so the question about cooked donkey hide seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The source showing that hide and placenta are not food unless prepared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: hide and placenta do not receive טומאת אוכלין, but cooked hide or a placenta someone intended to eat does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Food impurity, as it is taught: The hide and the placenta do not become impure with food impurity. A hide that someone cooked, and a placenta that someone intended to eat, do become impure with food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim that טומאת אוכלין was already taught. It quotes the ברייתא that gives this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hide and placenta are not normally eaten, so on their own they are not 'food' and cannot get food impurity. Once someone cooks the hide until it is edible, or plans to eat the placenta, they count as food. Since this rule is already stated, a new teaching about food impurity would be repeating it.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity that food can receive
Placenta, the afterbirth of an animal
Hide or skin
He cooked it (boiled it soft)
He intended it, meaning he planned to eat it

phrases.english: Food impurity, as it is taught:
The hide and the placenta –
do not become impure with food impurity,
a hide that one cooked,
and the placenta that one intended for eating –
do become impure with food impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the claim that food impurity was already taught
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a question about the food impurity of cooked hide would be unnecessary
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that hide and placenta get food impurity only when cooked or intended for eating

steps.title: The source showing that hide, bones and similar parts do not carry carcass impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא learning from the word 'בנבלתה' that the hide, bones, sinews, horns and hooves do not carry טומאת נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Carcass impurity was also already taught: 'Its carcass' – but not the hide, not its bones, not the sinews, not the horns, and not the hooves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second half of its challenge. It quotes the ברייתא showing that טומאת נבלות was already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says one who touches 'its carcass' becomes impure. The ברייתא reads that word narrowly: only the flesh counts, not the hide or the hard, inedible parts. Since this was already taught, a new teaching about carcass impurity would also seem to repeat it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Its carcass', the word in the פסוק that the rule is learned from
Bones
Sinews or tendons
Hooves

phrases.english: Carcass impurity we also already learned:
'Its carcass' – and not the hide,
and not its bones, and not the sinews,
and not the horns, and not the hooves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 2; supplies the source for the carcass-impurity half of the challenge
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a teaching about carcass impurity would be unnecessary
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'בנבלתה' to exclude hide, bones, sinews, horns and hooves

steps.title: The carcass-impurity teaching is needed for parts cooked into a pot-pudding
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנא explains that the ברייתא excluding hide and bones was needed only for a case where they were made into ציקי קדרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר רב חנא said: It was needed only for a case where one made them into a pot-pudding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנא explains why the ברייתא about carcass impurity was needed at all. It teaches something new only for the case where these parts were cooked into a pot-pudding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally it is obvious that hide and bones are not flesh. You might think that once they are cooked soft into a pudding, they become like flesh and carry טומאת נבלות, and the ברייתא teaches that even then they do not. That is why the גמרא quotes רבה בר רב חנא: even cooked hide is already covered for טומאת נבלות, which completes the challenge from Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for (this specific case)
A pot-pudding, a dish cooked for a long time with spices

steps.whatToRemember: Hide and placenta can become 'food' for טומאת אוכלין if cooked or intended for eating. But hide, bones, sinews, horns and hooves do not carry טומאת נבלות, even when cooked into ציקי קדרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that turning something into food is not enough to make it count as carcass flesh. The two impurities follow different rules.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Rav Ḥana said:
It was needed only
where one made them into a pot-pudding.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the parts just listed: the hide, bones, sinews, horns and hooves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the specific case the ברייתא in step 3 was needed for
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exclusion of hide, bones, sinews, horns and hooves from טומאת נבלות applies even when they were cooked into ציקי קדרה; that is the new point of the ברייתא.

steps.title: Donkey hide is different because it is disgusting
steps.stepSummary: The question really was about טומאת אוכלין. Even though the ברייתא already taught that cooked hide gets that טומאה, donkey hide might be different because it is repulsive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the question was about the טומאה of foods. Donkey hide is different, because it is disgusting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the earlier steps: why did anyone need to ask about cooked donkey hide if the ברייתא already covered cooked hide? It says the question was about טומאת אוכלין, and donkey hide is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said cooked hide counts as food for טומאת אוכלין. But that might only apply to normal hides. Donkey hide is so disgusting that maybe, even cooked, it is not considered food, so the question was still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to hold on to the original idea while giving a new explanation
The impurity that food can receive
It is different
Disgusting, repulsive

steps.whatToRemember: Even when a general rule is taught, something unusually disgusting (like donkey hide) may still need its own ruling about whether it counts as food.

phrases.english: Actually, the question was about the impurity of foods,
and donkey hide is different, because it is disgusting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא that both kinds of טומאה were already taught in the ברייתות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing a special case (donkey hide) from the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question about cooked donkey hide seemed unneeded, since the ברייתא already said cooked hide receives טומאת אוכלין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about טומאת אוכלין, and it is needed because donkey hide is disgusting and might not count as food even when cooked.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the rule of a placenta that came out
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה of a שליא that partly came out, רבי אלעזר says the משנה forbids it only when no fetus is found inside. If a fetus is inside, we do not worry about another fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the placenta that came out: רבי אלעזר said, they only taught this when there is no fetus with it. But if there is a fetus with it, we do not worry about another fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the words of the משנה, 'a placenta that came out.' רבי אלעזר explains when that rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids the placenta because maybe a fetus's head came out inside it. רבי אלעזר says that worry exists only if no fetus is found inside. If a fetus is found, we assume the placenta belonged to it, so there is no worry about some other fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: Placenta, the sac the fetus grows in
Fetus, unborn young
They only taught this (rule) in the case of...
We are concerned / we worry about a possibility

phrases.english: A placenta that came out.
Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין עִמָּהּ וָלָד,
phrases.english: They taught this only where there is no fetus with it,
but if there is a fetus with it,
we do not worry about another fetus.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁלְיָא שֶׁיָּצְתָה. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The placenta is forbidden only when no fetus is found inside; if one is found, there is no worry about another fetus.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says we always worry about another fetus
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: whether or not a fetus is found inside, we worry that the placenta belonged to another fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: whether there is no fetus with it or there is a fetus with it, we worry about another fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposing view to רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, finding a fetus inside does not remove the worry. Maybe there was a second fetus whose head came out in the placenta, so the placenta stays forbidden in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether... or... (in both cases)
Another fetus, besides the one found

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
whether there is no fetus with it
or there is a fetus with it,
we worry about another fetus.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בֵּין אֵין עִמָּהּ וָלָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר's leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In every case we worry about another fetus, so the placenta is forbidden.

steps.title: But רבי ירמיה said רבי אלעזר was being strict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this version: רבי ירמיה reported that רבי אלעזר's statement was a stringency, yet here it reads as a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי ירמיה said: רבי אלעזר said it as a stringency!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the way רבי אלעזר's opinion was just reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version above, רבי אלעזר is lenient (no worry if a fetus is inside) and רבי יוחנן is strict. But רבי ירמיה said רבי אלעזר's statement was strict. These two pictures cannot both be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (introduces a challenge)
But surely... (brings a contradicting source)
As a stringency, to be strict

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Yirmeya say:
Rabbi Elazar said it as a stringency!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reported wording of רבי אלעזר's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of רבי אלעזר's statement in step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ירמיה says רבי אלעזר's statement was strict, but the reported version makes it a leniency.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר restated: it depends on whether the placenta is attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבי אלעזר: the placenta is forbidden whenever it is not attached to the fetus inside. Only if it is attached do we not worry about another fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רבי אלעזר said: they taught this only when the placenta is not attached to the fetus. But if it is attached to the fetus, we do not worry about another fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a corrected version of what רבי אלעזר said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now just finding a fetus inside is not enough. Even with a fetus inside, the placenta is forbidden unless it is attached to that fetus. That makes רבי אלעזר's statement a stringency, matching רבי ירמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a statement)
Attached, connected

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, any fetus inside is enough to permit the placenta. In the corrected one, the placenta is permitted only if it is actually attached to the fetus inside.
steps.whatToRemember: Final version of רבי אלעזר: the placenta is forbidden even when a fetus is found inside, unless it is attached to that fetus.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְשׁוּרָה בַּוָּלָד,
phrases.english: They taught this only where it is not attached to the fetus,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the placenta, and 'the fetus' is the one found inside the womb.

phrases.english: but if it is attached to the fetus,
we do not worry about another fetus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rewording רבי אלעזר's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר permits the placenta whenever a fetus is found inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר forbids the placenta even with a fetus inside, unless it is attached to that fetus, which is a stringency.

steps.title: The reworded opinion of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: In the new version, רבי יוחנן says the placenta is forbidden only when no fetus at all is found. If any fetus is found, attached or not, we do not worry about another fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: the משנה forbids only a placenta with no fetus. If a fetus is with it, whether attached or not, we do not worry about another fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its fix from Step 9 and now gives the reworded opinion of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 7), רבי יוחנן was the strict one. Now the roles are flipped. רבי יוחנן is lenient: if any fetus is found, the placenta is assumed to be its own. רבי אלעזר is stricter, because he requires the placenta to be attached.

keyTerms.meaning: Placenta, the afterbirth
A fetus or newborn
Attached or tied, meaning the placenta is connected to the fetus
We are not concerned; we do not worry about this possibility

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 7. In the old version רבי יוחנן was strict. In this corrected version he is the lenient one.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
We have [the ruling] only
for a placenta without a fetus,
but if there is a fetus with it,
whether it is attached to the fetus
or whether it is not attached to the fetus,
we are not concerned about another fetus.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא שִׁלְיָא בְּלֹא וָלָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rewording begun in Step 9 by giving רבי יוחנן's side of the corrected מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the מחלוקת so that the roles of the two אמוראים are reversed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was the strict one, worrying about another fetus even when one was found.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן is lenient: any fetus found with the placenta removes the worry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A placenta is forbidden only when no fetus is found. If a fetus is found, attached or not, we do not worry about another fetus.

steps.title: The new version fits רבי ירמיה's report
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms that the reworded מחלוקת matches רבי ירמיה's statement that רבי אלעזר spoke as a stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי ירמיה meant: רבי אלעזר said his statement as a stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the loop and shows that the problem raised in Step 8 is now solved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8 the problem was that רבי אלעזר sounded lenient, while רבי ירמיה called him strict. Now that רבי אלעזר requires attachment and רבי יוחנן does not, רבי אלעזר really is the stricter one. So רבי ירמיה's report fits.

keyTerms.meaning: As a stringency, the stricter ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: רבי אלעזר says that without attachment we worry about another fetus, which is strict. רבי יוחנן says any fetus found is enough, which is lenient.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Rabbi Elazar said it as a stringency.
phrases.notes: This is the report the גמרא quoted back in Step 8. Now it finally fits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the rewording in Steps 9 and 10 answers the challenge from Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The corrected version, with רבי אלעזר as the strict one, matches רבי ירמיה's report.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when a woman miscarries an animal-shaped fetus with a placenta, an attached placenta raises no worry. An unattached placenta makes her keep the strictness of two births.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר: a woman who miscarries something shaped like an animal, a wild animal, or a bird, with a placenta, is not worried about another fetus if the placenta is attached. If it is not attached, I put on her the strictness of two births.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבי אלעזר's rule that attachment is what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not let the found fetus settle the matter by itself, which is what רבי יוחנן would say. It worries about another fetus unless the placenta is attached. That is exactly רבי אלעזר's line.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries
A form like a domesticated animal, a wild animal, or a bird
The strictness of two births, the strict side of both a boy's birth and a girl's birth

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a ברייתא as backing for the stricter, attachment-based view of רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rabbi Elazar:
A woman who miscarries a form of a domesticated animal, a wild animal, or a bird,
and a placenta is with them,
when it is attached to them,
we are not concerned about another fetus;
if it is not attached to them,
I place upon her
the stringency of two births.
phrases.notes: Since the missing baby might have been a boy or a girl, she keeps the stricter side of both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the wording, the גמרא brings outside support for רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's rule that only an attached placenta removes the worry about another fetus.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a woman who miscarries an animal-shaped fetus together with a placenta.

steps.title: The ברייתא's reason: something may have dissolved
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains its worry: perhaps the fetus that belonged to this placenta dissolved, and perhaps the placenta that belonged to the found fetus dissolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: For I say: perhaps the fetus of the placenta dissolved, and perhaps the placenta of the fetus dissolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason behind its strict ruling from Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The found fetus and the found placenta might not belong together. The placenta's own fetus, which may have had a human form, could have dissolved, and the found fetus's own placenta could also have dissolved. That is why only attachment proves they belong together.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally the fetal sac; here it means the fetus inside it
Dissolved, broke down and disappeared

phrases.english: For I say:
perhaps the fetus of the placenta dissolved,
perhaps the placenta of the fetus dissolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמַר: שֶׁמָּא נִימּוֹחַ שָׁפִיר שֶׁל שִׁלְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning inside the same ברייתא quoted in Step 12.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own explanation of a double dissolving.

steps.title: Why may the placenta of a first-time mother be thrown away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, an animal giving birth for the first time that expelled a placenta, and asks for the reason behind its ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: an animal giving birth for the first time that expelled a placenta. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its reason. It is setting up רב איקא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that this placenta may be thrown to the dogs, and we do not worry that it came from a holy firstborn that needs burial. The גמרא wants to know why we can be lenient here.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal giving birth for the first time, whose firstborn would have בכור status
What is the reason?

phrases.english: An animal giving birth for the first time that expelled [a placenta].
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says this placenta may be thrown to the dogs.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The discussion of a placenta found with a fetus has ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason we need not worry that the placenta belonged to a holy firstborn.

steps.title: רב איקא: most births are holy firstborns, a minority are נדמה
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בריה דרב אמי begins the answer: most animals give birth to something that gets firstborn holiness, while a minority give birth to a נדמה, which does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא son of רב אמי said: most animals give birth to something holy as a firstborn, and a minority give birth to something that is not holy as a firstborn. What is that? A נדמה, a baby that looks like another species.
steps.whatsHappening: רב איקא begins answering the question from Step 14 by setting out a majority and a minority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most first births look like their mother, which is the kind of animal that can get בכור holiness. A minority are a נדמה, which can never get firstborn holiness. This sets up the reasoning for why the placenta may be treated leniently. The גמרא continues building that reasoning in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Majority, most cases
Minority, fewer cases
Holy with firstborn status, a בכור
A look-alike: a baby shaped like a different species from its mother

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ika, son of Rav Ami, said:
Most animals give birth to
something that is holy with firstborn status,
and a minority of animals [give birth to]
something that is not holy with firstborn status,
and what is that? A look-alike.
phrases.notes: A נדמה is a baby born looking like a different species from its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי: רוֹב בְּהֵמוֹת יוֹלְדוֹת דָּבָר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בִּבְכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question asked in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer opens with a statistical setup: most first births are holy firstborns, and a minority are a נדמה, which is not holy.

steps.title: Females plus the minority make the males a minority
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא finishes his answer. Half of all young are female, and a minority are נדמה. Together these push the males that could be a בכור down to a minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, all animals that give birth have half males and half females. Put the small group of נדמה together with the half that are females, and the males turn out to be the minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why we don't worry that the placenta came from a holy firstborn. Most of the possible young could never have been a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a male that looks like its mother gets בכור holiness. Females never do, and a נדמה never does. So half (the females) plus a small extra group (the נדמה) is more than half. That leaves the possible בכור males as a minority, and we follow the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Half
Males
Females
Join the minority (to another group to make a majority)

steps.whatToRemember: Firstborn holiness goes only to a male that looks like its mother. Females plus the נדמה add up to a majority that is not holy, so the placenta is treated as not holy.

phrases.english: And all animals that give birth give birth to
half males and half females;
join the minority of the look-alikes
phrases.notes: נדמה is the animal from Step 15 that looks like a different species. It never gets firstborn holiness.

phrases.english: to the half that are females,
and the males become the minority.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הַיּוֹלְדוֹת יוֹלְדוֹת מֶחֱצָה זְכָרִים וּמֶחֱצָה נְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer that רב איקא began in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Females (half) plus the minority of נדמה are a majority, so the possible בכור males are a minority. That is why the placenta is not treated as holy.

steps.title: Why must a placenta from sacrificial animals be buried?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next ruling: with קדשים animals the placenta must be buried. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that with sacrificial animals, the placenta must be buried. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks why the placenta of a קדשים animal is treated as holy, so that it must be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The math from the last step showed that most young are not a בכור. So why should a placenta from קדשים be any different? The גמרא wants to know what changes the result.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside as sacrifices (קדשים)
It must be buried
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And with sacrificial animals, it must be buried.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ordinary firstborn case to the קדשים case in the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a placenta from קדשים is treated as holy and must be buried, when an ordinary first-birth placenta is not.

steps.title: Most young of sacrificial animals are holy
steps.stepSummary: Most of the young of קדשים animals can be holy, so the placenta is treated as holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The majority of them are fit to be holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that with קדשים, most of the young become holy. So we follow that majority and bury the placenta.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a בכור, only males count. With קדשים, both males and females born to the animal are holy. Only the small group of נדמה drops out, so now the holy young are the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority
Fit to become holy

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. With a בכור, females do not count. With קדשים, females are holy too. That is the whole difference.

phrases.english: The majority are fit to be holy.
phrases.notes: With קדשים, the females are holy too, so only the נדמה drop out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In קדשים both males and females are holy, so the majority of young are holy and the placenta must be buried.

steps.title: Healing purpose decides the rule of דרכי האמורי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on burying the placenta. אביי and רבא give a rule: anything with a healing purpose is not דרכי האמורי, and anything without one is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one may not bury it at a crossroads. אביי and רבא both said: anything that has healing in it is not forbidden as "the ways of the Amorite." Anything that has no healing in it is forbidden as "the ways of the Amorite."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a general rule to explain the משנה's ban. A practice is only forbidden as דרכי האמורי if it has no real healing purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה bans burying the placenta at a crossroads or hanging it on a tree because these are non-Jewish superstitions. אביי and רבא give the test: if something actually helps, it is allowed; if it is just superstition, it is forbidden. The placenta practices have no real benefit, so they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The ways of the Amorite: forbidden superstitious non-Jewish practices
Healing; a real medical or practical benefit
Both of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic test across הלכה for telling allowed practical remedies apart from forbidden superstitious practices.

phrases.english: But one may not bury it.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, which goes on: not at a crossroads, and not hung on a tree, because of the ways of the Amorite.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both said:
Anything that has healing in it
is not forbidden as the ways of the Amorite;
if it has no healing in it
it is forbidden as the ways of the Amorite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רְפוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה and explains it with a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A practice with a real healing benefit is not דרכי האמורי. A practice without one is forbidden as דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: A tree dropping its fruit seems to break the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי and רבא with a ברייתא. For a tree that drops its fruit too early, one may paint it red and load it with stones. The גמרא begins to explain that stones make sense, which suggests the red paint does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: a tree that drops its fruit too early may be painted with red paint and loaded with stones. It makes sense that one may load it with stones, so that...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. A ברייתא allows painting the tree red, which seems to have no real benefit. The גמרא is starting to explain why that is a problem for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loading the tree with stones has a clear practical reason, so it fits the rule. Red paint looks like it has no healing purpose, yet the ברייתא allows it. That would go against the rule of אביי and רבא. The sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that drops its fruit before they ripen
He paints it with red paint
He loads it with stones
Granted; this part makes sense (but the next part does not)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
A tree that drops its fruit too early,
one may paint it with red paint
and load it with stones.
Granted, loading it with stones makes sense,
so that...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of אביי and רבא from Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of אביי and רבא that a practice without healing value is forbidden as דרכי האמורי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows painting a tree red even though that seems to have no practical benefit, which goes against the rule.
